## Final candidate — data-grounded hypothesis

**Question:** In what centuries did we see the highest growth phase of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE?

**Hypothesis (headline: 1400s BCE):**
> The highest-growth phase of the 2000–1100 BCE interval occurred in the **1400s BCE (15th century BCE)**. Using the study's defined growth rate, **pollen_grate_100** (the percentage change of the 100-year-smoothed Belau/Woserin pollen openness score, **Belau_PC1**), the single peak growth rate (0.00465) falls at **~1415 BCE**, and the 1400s BCE also carries the **highest century-mean growth rate (+0.00193)** and the highest century-max of any century in the window. This peak is embedded in a broader, sustained upswing: the **longest contiguous run of positive growth spans ~1479–1364 BCE** (the 1400s BCE tailing into the 1300s BCE), with the 1400s and 1300s BCE the main above-average-growth centuries. Importantly, this "growth" is a **local upswing in the rate of landscape opening, not net growth**: the underlying smoothed openness index declines overall across the window (pollen_inter_100 falls from ~1.88 at 2000 BCE to ~1.07 at 1100 BCE). The reading is **corroborated by the archaeological capital record**, whose summed per-century Z-scores (capital.csv) peak sharply at **1400 BCE (Z-sum ≈ 11.3**, far above neighboring centuries).

Per your instruction, I do **not** label the 1500s BCE a positive-growth century (its century-mean was negative, −0.00302); the sustained positive run begins ~1479 BCE, the tail of the 1400s BCE.

## Evidence (from executed growth_analysis.py)
- **Window:** CE −2000…−1100 → 901 annual rows (time_series & pollen); 10 rows (capital). **0 NaN** in pollen_grate_100, pollen_inter_100, and all 12 capital Z-columns.
- **Peak (pollen_grate_100):** max 0.004650 at **CE −1415 (~1415 BCE)**.
- **Century means (BCE):** 1400s **+0.00193** (highest) > 1300s +0.00111 > 1600s +0.00087; 1500s −0.00302; 1100s −0.00105.
- **Longest positive-growth run:** CE −1479→−1364 = **BCE 1479–1364** (116 yrs); next CE −1341→−1241.
- **Overall trend:** pollen_inter_100 1.875 (2000 BCE) → 1.067 (1100 BCE) → net decline, so growth = local upswing.
- **Capital corroboration:** Z-sum peaks at **BCE 1400 = 11.28** (next: 1100→8.72, 1300→7.97, 1800→5.13).

## Workflow
Loaded time_series_data.csv (annual, CE −4100…−500), capital.csv (century-binned, comma decimals), and the Belau/Woserin pollen openness file (comma decimals). Restricted to the 2000–1100 BCE window (CE −2000…−1100; 901 annual rows; verified 0 NaN in the growth columns and capital Z-columns). Used **pollen_grate_100** as the study-defined growth rate: located the single peak (CE −1415, 0.00465) and aggregated to BCE centuries (1400s BCE = highest mean +0.00193 and max). Identified the longest contiguous positive-growth run (~1479–1364 BCE). Checked the overall pollen_inter_100 trend (net decline 1.88→1.07) to characterize growth as a local upswing. Corroborated with the capital.csv per-century Z-sum (peaks at BCE 1400, 11.28).

## One flag for you
You wrote "the **14th** century BCE (1400s BCE)." By standard convention the 1400s BCE (years 1499–1401 BCE) is the **15th century BCE** (the 14th c. BCE = the 1300s). I led with the unambiguous **"1400s BCE"** and annotated it as the 15th century BCE for accuracy. The data (peak ~1415 BCE, top century-mean in the 1400s bin) is unaffected — just the century ordinal. Say the word if you'd prefer I keep your "14th century" phrasing instead.
